P3885.note: The related data center is the Oracle campus near Abilene, Texas, which is part of the OpenAI Stargate effort. Crusoe is developing it on the 800 acre Lancium Clean Campus and leases about 90 acres. A Data Center Frontier article from March 2025 says the plan is eight buildings, about 4 million square feet and 1.2 GW in total, with the first two buildings over 200 MW. It says construction began in June 2024 and the full build was expected by mid-2026. An Energy Transfer earnings release from the third quarter of 2025 says it signed multiple long-term deals to supply about 900 million cubic feet a day of gas to three Oracle data centers, two of them in Texas. That release does not say how much of the gas goes to Abilene. An Energy Transfer executive quoted in an ETF Trends article from November 2025 calls Oracle a major customer in Abilene. Energy Transfer's second quarter 2026 release reports a second 14-mile lateral off the pipeline in Abilene. Data Center Frontier also says Crusoe lined up 4.5 GW of gas power with Engine No. 1, but does not clearly tie all of it to Abilene.

P7860.note: No single data center campus is named as the customer of this expansion. The Great Basin filing and Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo's February 2026 letter to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission say it would support existing customers and future economic development, including data centers. A Nevada Current article from June 2026 says the new line would run 14 miles to the Tahoe Regional Industrial Center in Storey County, Nevada. That industrial park has many data center projects but no source ties the pipeline to a specific one. Examples in the park are Fleet Data Centers, owned by Tract, with the Peru Ridge and South Valley campuses, and a Switch campus. A DatacenterDynamics article from September 2026 says Fleet asked for two gas plants totaling 360 MW to run its campuses until NV Energy can supply power. It says one Fleet data center is planned at 230 MW on 256 acres and that the tenant is not named. A Nevada Independent article from June 2026 says Nexus Fulcrum asked to build a 510 MW gas plant at the edge of the park. Switch acquired the site of that plant. None of these articles say they would take gas from this pipeline.

Fleet Data Centers campuses in the industrial park, 360 MW of gas plants, 230 MW campus, tenant not named

P8290.note: The related data center is Project Jupiter, a hyperscale campus at Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, New Mexico. Stack and BorderPlex Digital Assets are developing it. Oracle confirmed in January 2026 that it is the tenant and will host AI infrastructure for OpenAI. A DatacenterDynamics article from January 2026 says the campus covers 1,400 acres with four data center buildings, a microgrid, gas power plants, battery storage and a desalination plant. The developers have said they could invest up to $165 billion over the life of the project. Baxtel reported in July 2026 that the campus would run on up to 2.8 GW of Bloom solid oxide fuel cells, and its headline calls the campus 2.5 GW. The Albuquerque Journal says the air permit applicant is Yucca Growth Infrastructure LLC and the campus is under construction. The air permit is still being decided. Source New Mexico reported in April 2026 that the pipeline would carry 400,000 dekatherms a day to the private power plants for the campus, and in August 2026 that its start slipped to early 2027 after the state land office denied a route across state land.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The related data center is the Homer City Energy Campus in Center and Blacklick townships, Indiana County, Pennsylvania, on the site of the former Homer City coal plant. Homer City Redevelopment is building a 4.5 GW gas-fired power plant there, with Kiewit as builder and seven GE Vernova turbines. Developers put the first investment above $10 billion on a 3,200 acre site. A May 2026 local news report says construction began in April 2026 and the plant should produce power in 2028, while the 2025 announcement said 2027. Amazon Web Services said in August 2026 that it was in talks with the developer without a final deal. A DatacenterDynamics article from October 2026 says Amazon Data Services then filed a land development plan for 36 data center buildings on 1,100 acres. It says most of the plant's output would serve the campus and more than 1 GW would go to the grid. Earlier coverage named no tenant.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: No single data center campus is named for this expansion. The open season notice from Crossroads Pipeline Company, posted in February 2026, says the project responds to recently announced power generation and data center developments in the Midwest. It aims to serve markets in northern Indiana, Illinois, Iowa and South Dakota, with up to 1,500,000 dekatherms a day of capacity. Foundation shippers must commit at least 500,000 dekatherms a day for 20 years. Anchor shippers must commit at least 135,000 dekatherms a day for 20 years. The notice names no data center customer or shipper. The Energy Information Administration lists the demand served as power and data centers. A search found a $20 billion Joliet Technology Center in Illinois, but no source ties it to this project.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The related data center is Google's Project Roman campus in Hereford, Deaf Smith County, Texas. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from October 2026 says it starts with four buildings and that construction was expected to start in 2026. A report from the Amarillo television station KFDA in July 2026 says the project should bring about 2,500 construction jobs and about 90 permanent jobs, and the county judge said about 3,700 acres were bought. The shipper is IP Roman III Gas, an affiliate of Intersect Power, which Google bought in a $4.75 billion deal that closed in March 2026. It signed a 10-year agreement on April 9 for the full 550,000 dekatherms a day. The gas would fuel the proposed Roman Energy Center, up to 1.5 GW of gas engines. The air permit application also lists 462 MW of solar and 670 MW of wind. The filing does not name the end user. Natural Gas Intelligence says the governor halted Texas air permits pending an audit, which clouds the timeline.
